Random Walk Centrality

Source: R/centrality.R
centrality_random_walk.Rd

Random walk centrality of Noh and Rieger (2004), the stationary probability of a node over its characteristic relaxation time (their Eq. 10 and 11): $$C_i = \frac{P_i^\infty}{\tau_i}, \qquad \tau_i = \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \left(P_{ii}(t) - P_i^\infty\right),$$ where \(P_{ii}(t)\) is the probability that a walk started at \(i\) is back at \(i\) after \(t\) steps of a walk that moves to each out-neighbor with equal probability, and \(P_i^\infty\) its stationary probability (\(K_i / \sum_j K_j\) on an undirected network, Eq. 4).

Usage

centrality_random_walk(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The relaxation time is computed as \(\tau_i = Z_{ii} - P_i^\infty\) from the fundamental matrix \(Z = (I - P + W)^{-1}\) (Kemeny and Snell 1960), which is the series of Eq. 11 where it converges and its limit in the mean on a bipartite network, where the return probabilities oscillate. The reciprocal \(1 / C_j = \sum_i P_i^\infty m_{ij}\) is the mean first passage time into \(j\) from a start drawn from the stationary distribution, so differences of the reciprocals give the asymmetry of passage times, \(m_{ij} - m_{ji} = C_j^{-1} - C_i^{-1}\) (Eq. 9).

Edge weights are ignored, as in the paper. The paper treats undirected networks; on a strongly connected directed network the same Eq. 10 and 11 are evaluated with the stationary distribution of the directed walk. On any other network every score is NA, with a cograph_undefined_measure warning, because some passage times are infinite. tidygraph::centrality_random_walk() and netrankr's "dist_rwalk" with "invsum" report \(1 / \sum_i m_{ij}\), the unweighted sum of passage times into the node, which is not proportional to \(C_j\).

Before cograph 2.7.21 the score was \(1 / \sum_j (m_{ij} + m_{ji}) / 2\), which has no published source.

References

Noh, J. D. and Rieger, H. (2004). Random walks on complex networks. Physical Review Letters, 92(11), 118701. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.118701

Kemeny, J. G. and Snell, J. L. (1960). Finite Markov Chains. Van Nostrand.

See also

centrality_markov, centrality_current_flow_closeness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_random_walk(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.20932183 0.06088896 0.26259631 0.21855522 0.15238865 0.06853001 0.05111657 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.04409505 0.14373364 0.15987629
